jobs.title: OFW Services - Top Issues Program Manager-1
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
Project Management / Planning / Coordinating activities typically in the context of a production or services project to fulfill a business need according to financial/commercial parameters and ensuring customer satisfaction. Impacts quality, efficiency and effectiveness of own team. Has significant input into priorities. The role has moderate autonomy, requiring high levels of operational judgment

Job Description
Roles and Responsibilities
- Upon approval and acceptance of program,  be responsible for the whole scope of site activities from site mobilization to final acceptance, including but not limited to the co-ordinatation of  parts and labor
- Working with appropriate personnel, attain customer approval for implementation of the designated work scope.
- Work closely with engineering to ensure Work instructions and scope of programs are accurate and updates are incorporated.
- Ensure all safety requirements are met before execution is started, and any special LOTO procedures are developed.
- Establish and maintain performance metrics , specifically cost and schedule of implementation
- Identify and mitigate any potential barriers or delays in program execution.
- Regular cost debriefing to ensure budget of program is being met, taking any required actions as necessary if cost is exceeding estimates.
- Regular schedule updates in systems of records, to include completion and future schedule.
- Uses some judgment and has some ability to propose different solutions outside of standard scope to efficiently implement the program, such as bundling of multiple programs.
- Uses multiple internal and limited external sources outside of own teams to arrive at decisions.
- Comfortable with the challenges and different process of working within different countries for same program.
- Explains difficult or sensitive information; works to build consensus. Developing persuasion skills required to influence others on topics within field.
- Acts as a resource for colleagues with less experience.
- Will lead moderate to large scale programs, with programs ranging from 100 to 1000s of turbine.
- Ability to report progress and issues to multiple levels within the organization.
-

- Bachelor's degree from an accredited university or college (or a high school diploma / GED with at least 6 years of experience in Job Family Group(s)/Function(s)) or equivalent experience.
- Minimum of 1 years of experience in the Services & Retrofit/Upgrade in wind turbines.or
- Experience with ORACLE purchasing system/invoicing and debriefing systems.

Desired Characteristics
- Strong oral and written communication skills.
- Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems.
- Ability to document, plan, market, and execute programs.
- Established project management skills.
- Proficient in Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office suite
- Ability to multitask, prioritize and work effectively with virtual, global, remote team

jobs.title: Talent Acquisition Operations Manager (Americas)
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Talent Acquisition Operations Manager will lead a regional team of operations professionals for GE Vernova’s Talent Acquisition function across the Americas, providing leadership and operational oversight for Talent Acquisition processes, tools, analytics, lean, and compliance. Reporting to the Global Talent Acquisition Operations Leader, this role will oversee Lead and Senior TA Operations team members and drive regional execution in support of a standardized, high-quality, and efficient hiring experience.

The TA Operations Manager will play a critical role in translating global TA Operations strategy into effective regional delivery across the Americas. In partnership with recruiting teams, stakeholders, and cross-functional partners, this role will help advance Talent Acquisition capabilities, improve process adoption, strengthen stakeholder experience, and foster a culture of team, belonging, and growth.

Job Description
Essential Responsibilities
- Lead regional initiatives and priorities that strengthen Talent Acquisition Operations capabilities and support continuous improvement across the Americas
- Manage a regional team of TA Operations professionals, including Lead and Senior team members and coordinators, to deliver high-quality outcomes on time in a fast-paced environment
- Drive regional adoption of recruiting processes, enterprise standards, tools, and technologies
- Monitor regional metrics, workload, capacity, service delivery, and data integrity to identify trends, risks, and opportunities
- Leverage data and analytics to reinforce accountability and improve operational performance
- Partner with recruiting teams and stakeholders to improve the candidate, recruiter, and hiring leader experience
- Apply Lean methodologies and project management rigor to process improvements and operational enhancements
- Partner with technology teams on implementation, support, training, and adoption of recruiting tools and systems
- Oversee compliance with company policies, data privacy regulations, enterprise standards, and local requirements across the Americas region
- Support governance activities, including audits, controls, and regional compliance reviews
- Serve as the regional point of contact for escalations and stakeholder needs related to TA Operations
- Contribute to global TA Operations projects and share regional insights to support enterprise-wide improvements
- Foster a culture of belonging, growth, accountability, and continuous improvement

Basic Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university or college, or equivalent knowledge/experience

- Minimum (12) years of experience in Talent Acquisition with a minimum of (10) years of experience in Talent Acquisition Operations

- Minimum of (5) years of People Leadership experience

- Prior experience managing people and/or leading high-performing teams

- Experience leading cross-functional, remote, and diverse teams or initiatives

- Expertise in recruiting best practices, process improvement, project and change management, and recruiting technologies and systems

- Strong analytical skills and experience using data to support decisions and improve outcomes

- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel

- Willingness to work across multiple time zones within the Americas and on select global calls as needed

- Willingness to travel up to 10% as required

- Strong English language proficiency (speaking, writing, and reading)

- Ability to prioritize tasks and adapt as priorities evolve

Desired Characteristics
- Proven success leading teams to achieve high-quality outcomes
- Proven success managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Results-oriented with strong attention to detail
- Strong collaboration and influencing skills across stakeholders and organizational levels
- Demonstrated ability to build consensus and drive adoption of change
- Continuous improvement mindset and strong operational discipline

The salary range for this position is $122,400 to $203,900 USD Annual. The specific salary offered to a candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including the candidate’s experience, their education, and the work location. In addition, this position is eligible for a 15% performance bonus.

*The Company pays a geographic differential of 110%, 120% or 130% of salary in certain areas.

jobs.title: Repair Lean Leader
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Senior Lean & Operational Excellence Leader is a key member of the Plant Leadership Team and reports directly to the Plant Leader. This role is responsible for establishing and leading the Lean and Operational Excellence strategy for a new greenfield manufacturing facility supporting approximately 600 employees within a global energy manufacturing organization.
The Senior Lean & Operational Excellence Leader will help build the site's operating system from the ground up, embedding Lean principles into facility design, manufacturing processes, material flow, daily management, problem solving, and leadership practices. The role will lead a team of Lean/Continuous Improvement professionals and partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, EHS, Finance, and other functions to deliver measurable improvements in Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, and People capability.
This is a highly visible leadership role with significant influence on the culture, operating model, and long-term performance of the new facility.

Job Description
The Senior Lean & Operational Excellence Leader is a key member of the Plant Leadership Team and reports directly to the Plant Leader. This role is responsible for establishing and leading the Lean and Operational Excellence strategy for a new greenfield manufacturing facility supporting approximately 600 employees within a global energy manufacturing organization.
The Senior Lean & Operational Excellence Leader will help build the site's operating system from the ground up, embedding Lean principles into facility design, manufacturing processes, material flow, daily management, problem solving, and leadership practices. The role will lead a team of Lean/Continuous Improvement professionals and partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, EHS, Finance, and other functions to deliver measurable improvements in Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, and People capability.
This is a highly visible leadership role with significant influence on the culture, operating model, and long-term performance of the new facility.
Key Responsibilities
- Lead the site's Lean & Operational Excellence strategy: Develop and execute the Lean roadmap and Operating System in partnership with the Plant Leader and Plant Leadership Team, aligning priorities to business objectives and measurable SQDC performance.
- Build the greenfield operating system: Embed Lean principles into facility design, manufacturing processes, material flow, equipment, automation, standard work, and management systems to establish a scalable, high-performing operation from launch.
- Drive manufacturing performance: Lead initiatives that improve Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, productivity, throughput, capacity, lead time, inventory, and overall equipment effectiveness, with a clear focus on sustainable business results.
- Establish daily management and performance systems: Deploy strategy deployment, daily management, leader standard work, visual management, Gemba routines, and escalation processes that enable leaders and teams to identify and resolve performance gaps quickly.
- Lead continuous improvement and problem solving: Direct Kaizen, Action Work Outs, value-stream improvement, and structured problem-solving activities that eliminate waste, variation, bottlenecks, and process complexity.
- Develop Lean capability and leadership: Lead, coach, and develop the Lean/Continuous Improvement team while building Lean, problem-solving, and continuous improvement capability across all levels of the organization.
- Integrate Lean into product and process development: Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and other functions to incorporate Lean principles into new product introduction, industrialization, process development, equipment selection, and capacity expansion.
- Enable digital and technology transformation: Partner with Engineering, IT, and Operations to leverage automation, digital tools, analytics, and smart manufacturing technologies that simplify processes and improve safety, quality, flow, productivity, and decision making.
- Drive cross-functional alignment: Serve as a strategic partner to Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, EHS, Finance, HR, and other functions to align resources and accelerate operational improvements across the site.
- Ensure benefits realization: Establish clear improvement targets, ownership, milestones, and sustainment plans, and partner with Finance to quantify and validate productivity, cost, capacity, and other business benefits.
- Build a culture of ownership and continuous improvement: Develop an environment where employees at every level are empowered to identify problems, improve processes, and sustain gains, with leaders accountable for developing people and improving performance.
- Champion Safety, Quality, and operational discipline: Ensure Lean initiatives reinforce an uncompromising commitment to EHS, quality, compliance, and customer requirements, including immediate intervention and stop-work authority when serious safety risks are identified.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related discipline.
- 7+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, Lean, Continuous Improvement, Operational Excellence, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications
- Master's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or an MBA.
- Lean Six Sigma Black Belt, Lean certification, or equivalent experience.
- Demonstrated experience leading Lean deployment and delivering measurable improvements in manufacturing performance.

- Demonstrated experience leading and developing Lean/Continuous Improvement professionals or cross-functional teams.
- Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing and Six Sigma principles, including strategy deployment, daily management, value-stream mapping, standard work, Kaizen, structured problem solving, pull/flow, visual management, 5S, error proofing, and TPM.
- Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional transformation initiatives.
- Strong business and financial acumen, including the ability to connect operational improvements to measurable business results.
- Strong communication, facilitation, coaching, and executive presentation skills.
- Demonstrated ability to influence organizational change across multiple functions and levels.
- Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, highly matrixed manufacturing environment.

- Experience launching or transforming a greenfield manufacturing facility.
- Experience in energy, industrial, aerospace, power generation, heavy manufacturing, or another complex manufacturing environment.
- Experience with manufacturing automation, digital transformation, MES, advanced analytics, or smart manufacturing.
- Experience integrating Lean principles into product development, industrialization, and new product introduction.
- Experience with benefits realization and financial validation of improvement initiatives.
- Strong understanding of production planning, inventory management, quality systems, standard cost, capacity planning, and capital investment.
- Experience working successfully within a large, complex, global organization.

Success in the Role
Success will be demonstrated through:
- Achievement of site Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, and People objectives.
- Improved throughput, flow, lead time, capacity, labor productivity, and customer delivery.
- Sustainable reductions in inventory, waste, variation, and operating cost.
- Strong first-pass yield and right-first-time performance.
- Development of a capable and engaged Lean organization and broader problem-solving culture.
- Effective integration of Lean principles into facility design, equipment, automation, and manufacturing processes.
- Sustained employee engagement and ownership of continuous improvement.
- Demonstrated financial and operational value from Lean and Operational Excellence initiatives.

jobs.title: Materials Lean Leader
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Materials Lean Leader will provide support and coaching within the Supply chain focused on the development and sustainment of a Materials Management Strategy (roadmap) aligned with the business targets. You will partner with organizational leadership to drive product and process improvements that deliver lead time and inventory reductions supporting customer delivery.

Job Description
Essential Responsibilities:
As the Materials Lean Leader you will:
- Develop and execute the lean roadmap for the materials organization, ensuring alignment and synergy between internal materials planning and operations.
- Collaborate with planners to integrate them into the Pull/replenishment systems, fostering seamless supply chain operations and alignment with internal processes.
- Facilitate regular communication and feedback loops between the internal factory and external suppliers to ensure consistent application of lean principles.
- Own priorities for parts on pull and schedule attainment aligned with business targets
- Responsible for continuous improvement plans for materials lean systems including VSMs
- Coach teams from front line to executives on lean materials systems
- Plan and deliver projects & initiatives aligned to the roadmap

Qualifications/Requirements:
- Bachelor's Degree from an accredited university or college (or a high school diploma /GED with at least 10 years of experience in Manufacturing)
- Minimum of 5 additional years in Lean and/or Materials

Desired Characteristics:
- Proven ability to collaborate with external partners and integrate them into existing systems to enhance overall supply chain efficiency.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills to effectively manage relationships
- Change agent with strong credibility and influence in the organization
- Lean Materials experience including but not limited to: standard work, material presentation, supermarkets, flow, pull, waterspider routes, heijunka, and kanban

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
IT Leader managing the Services Outage Execution portfolio. Directs field readiness initiatives, ensuring employees have the necessary connectivity and equipment for onsite work. Leads programs to enhance field productivity and data accessibility in support of customer outage commitments.

Job Description
In this role, you will proactively and holistically help guide business and IT teams through transformation and optimization initiatives, supporting the formation of strategy using Services value stream framework.

Global Services delivers post Implementation services to external customers In areas of CSA, Outage Management and Projects Services globally.

As a IT Leader managing the Services Outage Execution portfolio for Gas Power Global Services, you will be accountable for the following priorities (including leading a team):
1. Portfolio & Process Governance
- - End-to-End Ownership:  Serve as the strategic owner for the Services Outage Execution process and its associated application portfolio.
- Lifecycle Management:  Oversee the performance, maintenance, and optimization of critical applications supporting outage workflows.
- Continuous Improvement:  Evaluate current processes to identify gaps, ensuring IT solutions evolve to meet changing business requirements.

2. Field Operations & Readiness
- - Infrastructure Logistics:  Lead the proactive provisioning and lifecycle management of IT equipment, including hardware and PC availability for a mobile, customer-facing workforce.
- Site Connectivity:  Ensure robust onsite connectivity solutions are defined and implemented, guaranteeing that field teams have the bandwidth and network stability required to complete GE Vernova work.
- Readiness Standards:  Establish and enforce deployment protocols that ensure field employees are fully "site-ready" before arriving at customer locations.

3. Strategic Productivity & Innovation
- - Program Leadership:  Drive the identification, business case development, and execution of technology programs focused on increasing the output and efficiency of field personnel.
- Use of AI to drive productivity:  Lead efforts to improve data accessibility and visibility, ensuring field teams have the right information at the right time to meet complex customer commitments.
- Solution Delivery:  Translate business challenges into technical solutions, managing program delivery from concept through to field implementation.

4. Stakeholder & Customer Impact
- - Commitment Alignment:  Ensure all IT-led initiatives are directly tied to the successful delivery of outage milestones and customer satisfaction.
- Cross-Functional Collaboration:  Partner with operations and field service leaders to advocate for and deliver the technology needed for successful site execution.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's Degree in   Information Technology areas with minimum 10 years of relevant experience

Desired Characteristics

- Proven track record of setting targets, executing a plan, and delivering results
- Relevant experience with demonstrated solving of business problems with technology
- Ability to plan and provide structure and organization in a fast paced, changing environment
- Effectively manages risk and uncertainty for self and team.
- Strong business analysis and problem-solving skills
- Ability to decompose problems and make decisions when problems or solutions are not 100% defined
- Evaluates products & processes to assure compliance.
- Measures the impact of trends (cyclical or a shift) and takes action.
- Ability to interact at all levels of the organization, and with other GE businesses and partners

- Proactively identifies and removes project obstacles or barriers on behalf of the team

jobs.title: OFS FP&A Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
This is a global position on the One Field Services (OFS) Finance team for the Gas Power Global Services business. The role is focused on enhancing the field services SIOP process from a financial standpoint and drives the implementation of global standard processes across the regions (ITRs & OFS). Partnering with the OFS FP&A team to understand the Services COGS output from OFS and GTM, this individual owns the maintenance, enhancement, and prioritization of ITR tool and supporting systems — including Astro — and drives the analytics and operating standards that raise performance across the business. It requires an in-depth understanding of the field services fulfillment model, strong cross-functional partnership, and a blend of finance and systems acumen.

Job Description
What you will do

- Astro Ownership & Data Governance: Act as the functional owner for Field Services ITR tool (Astro). Partner with IT to prioritize system enhancements and drive automation of manual reporting processes. This includes managing critical integrations between Event Vision & ISM to ensure accurate pacing and reporting data.

- Process Strategy & Transformation: Lead the design and cross-functional implementation of global operating standards for Field Services fulfilments and support SIOP process enhancements to drive business transformation and improve profitability.

- Financial Planning, Forecasting & Reporting: Support Services planning, pacing, monthly close and reporting cycles, ensuring financials accuracy and timely KPI reporting. Leverage deep cost expertise to produce reliable short- and medium-term forecasts by correlating recent trends with underlying base-cost drivers.

- Analytics & Cross-Functional Integration: Partner with Global Services FP&A, Operations and region ITR stakeholders to bridge the gap between operational output and financial results. Utilize data analytics to monitor performance, improve cost visibility, and ensure full cost liquidation across the business.

What you will bring (Basic Qualifications)
- Bachelor's degree in accounting, Finance, or Business Administration or equivalent experience.
- Minimum of 5 years of financial work experience in a global business environment.
- Strong analytical, project management, and organizational skills.
- Ability to work under tight deadlines and to prioritize under pressure.
- Proven record of consistently meeting and frequently exceeding expectations.
- Proactive in driving results in a fast-paced environment.
- Operational mindset, with an interest in developing finance and business acumen.
- Strong oral and written communication skills.

What will make you stand out
- Preferred graduate of finance management leadership programs (e.g., FMP, OFLP/CAS, etc.)
- A passion for collaborating cross-functionally to solve complex operational and financial problems.

jobs.title: Senior Finance Manager, Supply Chain, Wind Services
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Senior Manager, Supply Chain Finance for Wind Services will serve as a key financial leader, providing strategic decision support and rigorous financial oversight for the global Supply Chain organization. This role is responsible for driving the financial performance of our remanufacturing and supply chain operations, with a specific focus on the operationalization of remanufacturing strategies, structural cost management, and inventory / footprint optimization.

Job Description
Key Responsibilities
Global FP&A for Supply Chain
- Lead the comprehensive financial planning, budgeting, and forecasting processes for the global Wind Services supply chain.
- Provide actionable insights into cost drivers, manufacturing variances, and overhead absorption to drive P&L performance.
- Partner with supply chain leadership to translate operational KPIs into financial outcomes, ensuring alignment with annual and long-range business objectives.

Remanufacturing Strategy & Implementation
- Act as the financial architect for the Remanufacturing operations, leading the business case development for new site ramps, technology investments, and process scaling.
- Support the transition from pilot to full-scale operations, ensuring robust cost-accounting models are in place for refurbished components.
- Monitor and report on the profitability of remanufacturing vs. new-make components to influence service life-cycle strategy.

Structural Cost Management & Optimization
- Develop and execute a global structural cost management framework, identifying opportunities to reduce fixed and variable cost intensity across the supply chain.
- Lead analytical efforts related to global manufacturing footprint optimization, including location strategy, lease/buy decisions, and capacity planning.
- Oversee inventory strategy to drive improvements in Working Capital, balancing supply reliability with optimal inventory turns and valuation health.

Strategic Analysis & Controllership
- Conduct high-impact ad hoc financial modeling to support executive decision-making on sourcing strategy, logistics network design, and capital allocation.
- Maintain rigorous controllership, ensuring all supply chain financial practices remain in compliance with US GAAP and corporate accounting policies.
- Cultivate a data-driven, innovative culture by leveraging advanced visualization tools (Tableau/Power BI) and automation techniques (Python/n8n/SQL) to provide real-time visibility into supply chain risks and opportunities.

Qualifications & Requirements
- Education:  Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Mathematics, or Engineering; MBA or professional certification (CPA/CMA/CFA) preferred.
- Experience:  5+ years of progressive experience in Supply Chain Finance, Plant Finance, or Operational FP&A, preferably within the industrial or energy sector.
- Technical Expertise:  Expert-level proficiency in financial modeling, ERP systems (SAP/Oracle), modern data analysis (Python, SQL, etc.) and data visualization tools (Tableau/PowerBI).

jobs.title: Senior Lean Manager / Responsable Lean - Gas Value Stream (H/F)
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
Are you ready to accelerate the energy transition by driving operational excellence? At GE Vernova, we are building a world that works. As our Senior Lean Manager for the Gas Value Stream, you will lead our operational transformation, placing Lean principles and the Toyota Production System (TPS) at the heart of our industrial performance.

Job Description
*** EN FRANCAIS PLUS BAS ***

Key Responsibilities
You will play a critical role in:
- Driving Lean Transformation:   Lead the deployment of Lean strategy across Gas manufacturing facilities, in alignment with GE Vernova’s operational priorities and Global Supply Chain standards.

- Leading High-Impact Kaizen Events:   Plan and execute Kaizen events focused on flow, lead time reduction, productivity, and defect elimination—delivering measurable, sustainable results.

- Coaching & Capability Building:   Partner with site leaders and cross-functional teams to build Lean capability, providing hands-on coaching in Daily Management, problem-solving, and continuous improvement.

- Advancing Built-In Quality (BIQ):   Lead BIQ deployment to embed defect prevention into processes through standardized work, error-proofing, and process control.

- Scaling Best Practices:   Identify, standardize, and deploy best practices across Gas sites to accelerate Lean maturity and ensure consistency across the Gas network.

Candidate Profile
We are looking for a change agent with:
- Education:   Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field.

- Experience:   Significant experience in Lean Manufacturing within a complex industrial or heavy manufacturing environment, with a proven track record of leading site-wide transformation initiatives.

- Lean / TPS Expertise:   Strong hands-on experience implementing TPS principles (laminar flow, Jidoka, pull systems/Kanban, TPM, single-piece flow).

- Innovation:   Practical experience with lean innovations such as Moonshine systems and Karakuri-based automation.

- Influence & Leadership:   Strong ability to influence, coach, and drive cultural transformation across diverse, multi-site organizations, engaging shop-floor teams and senior leadership alike.

Preferred Qualifications: Prior experience working with Shingijutsu, Toyota, or equivalent world-class Lean organizations is a strong advantage, as is experience in heavy industry (e.g., gas turbines, large equipment).

*** VERSION FRANCAISE ***

Vous souhaitez accélérer la transition énergétique en transformant l'excellence opérationnelle ? Chez GE Vernova, nous construisons un monde qui fonctionne. En tant que Responsable Lean pour notre division Gas, vous serez le moteur de notre transformation opérationnelle, en plaçant le Lean et le système de production Toyota (TPS) au cœur de notre performance industrielle.

Vos missions principales   En tant que membre clé de notre organisation, vous aurez pour mission de :
- Piloter la transformation Lean :   Déployer notre stratégie Lean sur l'ensemble de nos sites de production Gas, en alignement avec les standards globaux de la Supply Chain.

- Animer la performance par les Kaizen :   Planifier et diriger des événements Kaizen à fort impact pour optimiser les flux, réduire les délais de production et éliminer les gaspillages, tout en garantissant des résultats durables.

- Développer les compétences Lean :   Accompagner les équipes de direction de site et les fonctions transverses dans l'appropriation des pratiques de management quotidien (Daily Management), de résolution de problèmes et d'amélioration continue.

- Renforcer la culture "Qualité Intégrée" (BIQ) :   Déployer les standards BIQ pour ancrer la prévention des défauts dans nos processus grâce au travail standardisé et au contrôle des procédés.

- Standardiser et déployer les meilleures pratiques :   Harmoniser les méthodes à travers nos sites pour accélérer la maturité Lean et favoriser une culture unifiée au sein du réseau Gas.

Profil recherché   Nous recherchons une personne passionnée par l'excellence opérationnelle, possédant :
- Formation :   Un diplôme d'études supérieures (Bachelor ou équivalent) en ingénierie, gestion des opérations ou domaine connexe.

- Expérience :   Une expérience significative en environnement manufacturier complexe ou industrie lourde, avec une expertise démontrée dans le déploiement de transformations Lean.

- Expertise Lean / TPS :   Une maîtrise pratique des principes du Toyota Production System (flux, Jidoka, systèmes tirés/Kanban, TPM, flux pièce à pièce).

- Innovations :   Une capacité à mettre en œuvre des solutions d'automatisation pratiques (type Moonshine ou Karakuri).

- Leadership :   Une forte capacité à influencer, coacher et fédérer des équipes, du terrain jusqu'à la direction, dans un contexte multisite.

Atout supplémentaire : Une expérience préalable au sein d'organisations Lean de classe mondiale (type Shingijutsu ou Toyota) ainsi qu'une expérience spécifique dans l'industrie des turbines ou équipements lourds sont des atouts précieux.

Additional Information
Relocation Assistance Provided: Yes

jobs.title: Directeur régional des ventes et de la stratégie pour les éoliennes/Regional Wind Turbine Sales and Strategy Director
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
Ce poste représente une fonction de direction stratégique au sein de GE Vernova, exigeant une maîtrise combinant vision à long terme et exécution commerciale rigoureuse. Le titulaire est responsable de piloter la croissance rentable du portefeuille éolien terrestre par le développement des ventes d’éoliennes et des services associés. Au-delà du pilotage du cycle de vie complet des contrats — de la prospection initiale à la clôture financière — ce rôle implique une orchestration transversale complexe. Le gestionnaire doit en effet fédérer des équipes multidisciplinaires (ingénierie, chaîne d’approvisionnement, finance, exécution) pour aligner les capacités techniques de GE avec les besoins spécifiques des clients. Avec un périmètre prioritaire couvrant le Canada et le Nord-Est des États-Unis, le candidat idéal devra démontrer une fine compréhension des enjeux réglementaires régionaux, une capacité à créer une demande durable pour nos technologies et une aptitude à influencer les parties prenantes internes afin de garantir l'excellence opérationnelle et la valeur ajoutée pour nos clients.

The Senior Wind Turbine Sales and Strategy Manager for GE Onshore Wind, a business unit of GE Vernova, is responsible for driving profitable growth in the onshore wind portfolio through increasing sales of GE's world-class wind turbines and associated services. In this role, you will develop the sales and customer growth strategies, maintain existing customer relationships, develop new clients, create product demand, and own assign accounts and markets from opportunity creation to thru contract closure. You will also need to work closely with product management, services, supply chain, finance commercial operations, engineering, and project execution teams. Assigned accounts and new account prospecting is expected to be primarily in Canada and the Northeast U.S.

Job Description
L'activité éolien terrestre de GE Vernova dispose d'une base installée totale de plus de 50 000 éoliennes dans plus de 35 pays, représentant une capacité installée mondiale supérieure à 100 GW. Nous exploitons le potentiel croissant de l'énergie éolienne terrestre grâce à une vaste gamme d'éoliennes parfaitement adaptées à divers environnements, notamment la plateforme de 6 MW de GE — notre éolienne terrestre la plus puissante — et notre plateforme de 4 MW, qui s'impose comme la nouvelle turbine de référence. Nous nous engageons à assurer la réussite de nos clients dans le secteur éolien en proposant un large portefeuille de produits et de services qui font des énergies renouvelables le choix énergétique privilégié pour un avenir plus propre.

Responsabilités essentielles :
- Développer et piloter la stratégie   d'entrée sur le marché et de croissance pour les comptes assignés, incluant le plan d'affaires et les objectifs de KPI pluriannuels (ex : commandes, marge, trésorerie, etc.).
- Identifier, développer et conclure   des opportunités de vente avec les comptes assignés sur le territoire défini.
- Créer et entretenir des relations étroites   avec les interlocuteurs clés des comptes assignés afin de comprendre leurs stratégies et besoins.
- Prospecter et développer   de nouveaux comptes pour élargir la base clients.
- Agir en tant que partenaire de confiance   et propriétaire de la relation exécutive, en adoptant une approche consultative axée sur l'apport d'insights stratégiques.
- Fournir une assistance commerciale et technique   pour soutenir le développement des stratégies énergétiques renouvelables des clients via les solutions GE Vernova.
- Assurer la position favorable des produits et services GE   dans tous les projets, de l'identification à la clôture de transactions complexes (plusieurs centaines de millions).
- Analyser l'impact des marchés   nationaux et régionaux, du financement et de la compétitivité des offres GE.
- Assurer une veille concurrentielle et réglementaire   afin de traduire les tendances en recommandations stratégiques (prix, planification).
- Communiquer la valeur ajoutée   des nouveaux produits et services éoliens terrestres de GE aux comptes assignés.
- Promouvoir une culture orientée client   et représenter la "voix du client" en interne pour influencer la feuille de route produit.
- Travailler en équipe multidisciplinaire   (Opérations commerciales, Ingénierie, Sourcing, Finance, Exécution de projet) pour exécuter des stratégies gagnantes.
- Représenter l'entreprise   auprès des associations industrielles, des parties prenantes gouvernementales et des organismes politiques.
- Aligner les stratégies régionales   avec les objectifs globaux de l'entreprise.
- Participer aux salons et conférences   du secteur des énergies renouvelables.
- Maintenir des données précises   dans l'outil Salesforce et gérer le processus ITO (Inquiry to Order).
- Gérer les KPIs du territoire   (engagements, commandes, rentabilité, risques, conditions contractuelles).

Qualifications et exigences :
- Diplôme universitaire   (Licence/Bachelor) en ingénierie ou en commerce.
- Minimum de 10 ans d'expérience   : vente d'équipements lourds et/ou de services à long terme (secteur de la production d'énergie privilégié), négociation de contrats complexes, développement de stratégies commerciales.
- Maîtrise courante de l'anglais et du français.
- Localisation :   Nord-Est des États-Unis, Québec ou Ontario.

Caractéristiques souhaitées :
- Localisation préférée :   Québec ou Ontario (ou volonté de relocalisation).
- Master   en ingénierie ou en commerce.
- Connaissance approfondie   de l'industrie de la production d'énergie au Canada et/ou aux États-Unis.
- Expérience démontrée   dans le développement d'une base clients à partir de zéro.
- Réseau établi   dans le secteur éolien ou dans le domaine des équipements lourds.
- Approche de vente "Challenger"   : capacité à façonner la réflexion du client sur la stratégie de projet et l'économie du projet.
- Compétences en négociation :   rigueur factuelle et financière pour défendre les termes contractuels.
- Esprit entrepreneurial :   dynamisme, optimisme et discipline dans une organisation matricielle globale.
- Connaissance des enjeux réglementaires et réseau :   compréhension pointue du contexte éolien en Amérique du Nord.
- Présence exécutive :   capacité à représenter l'entreprise au plus haut niveau (C-Suite).
- Disponibilité :   Capacité et volonté de voyager au moins 50 % du temps.
- Maîtrise des outils :   Salesforce et suite Microsoft Office.

GE Vernova’s Onshore Wind business has a total installed base of more than 50,000 wind turbines in more than 35 counties, with 100+ GW of global installed capacity. We harness increased onshore wind energy potential through a broad family of turbines that are uniquely suited for a variety of wind environments, including: GE’s 6MW turbine platform, GE’s most powerful onshore wind turbine and our 4MWturbine Platform as the next workhorse turbine. We are committed to our customers’ success in wind, offering a broad portfolio of products and services that make renewables the energy of choice for a cleaner future.

- Minimum of 10 years of relevant experience including: selling capital equipment and/or long-term services (preferably within the power generation industry), developing complex commercial proposals, negotiating complex contracts, developing market strategies and business plans leading to a scalable region/business.

- Demonstrated success using a Challenger-style, insight-led selling approach; ability to act as a genuine senior partner to customer leadership and to shape customer thinking on project strategy and economics

The Executive Director, Enterprise Strategy will report to the executive leader of the Strategy & Portfolio team within the Corporate Strategy & Market Analytics organization, and will partner with leaders across GE Vernova’s corporate and business unit teams to lead strategy projects.

Job Description
- Enterprise Strategy - Drive strategic impact by co-leading a cross-functional process to identify the top corporate-level strategic opportunities or risks facing GE Vernova, and leading strategic analyses to address them - Play a key role in developing enterprise growth initiatives, including identifying, assessing, and prioritizing adjacent markets GE Vernova could enter

- Work closely with the market analytics team to translate market intelligence into actionable strategic insights
- Prepare high-quality presentations and memos summarizing the findings and recommendations, and facilitate senior executive-level discussions to drive buy-in and alignment

- Collaborate closely with GE Vernova’s Corporate Business Development team in developing and evaluating strategic choices of acquisitions and/or divestitures
- Contribute to capital allocation decisions of organic investments and M&A

- Collaborate with an ecosystem comprised of technology strategy, segment strategy, R&D and business units to accelerate growth strategy from ideation to commercialization

​

Across these projects the Executive Director, Enterprise Strategy will:

- Secure buy-in from executive stakeholders across the organization and orchestrate contributions from junior team members and virtual teams
- Contribute to talent development and knowledge transfer to advance the capabilities of the corporate team
- Conduct rigorous quantitative analyses with actionable recommendations

- Experience leading a corporate strategic planning process, growth strategy development and M&A strategy formulation

jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
Do you want to drive the future of energy infrastructure by shaping the technologies that power our world?

GE Vernova is looking for an exceptional Aero Alliance Industrialization Program Manager to join our Aero Alliance team based in Carrara.

Job Description
GE Vernova - The Energy to Change the World
With over 130 years of experience and proven innovation, GE Vernova is leading a new era of energy. We are electrifying the world while working to decarbonize it. Our name reflects our mission. “GE” carries a legacy of quality and ingenuity. “Ver” signals Earth’s lush ecosystems, while “Nova” nods to a new era of lower-carbon energy we are helping to deliver.
Focused on the future, GE Vernova is accelerating the shift to reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy. We help customers power economies and deliver electricity vital to health, safety, and quality of life.

Power
Our Power portfolio provides sustainable, more efficient energy solutions. With expertise across Gas, Hydro, Nuclear, and Steam Power, we help customers deliver electricity to homes, industries, and communities worldwide.

Let’s Talk about the Role
The Aero Alliance Industrialization Program Manager will lead the execution of new repair capabilities and industrialization projects to optimize product performance and turnaround times.
You will act as the primary bridge between engineering teams, repair shops, and external suppliers, building business cases and managing the lifecycle of industrialization activities. Your focus will be on driving cost-out initiatives and technological advancements that enhance the value and efficiency of our aeroderivative gas turbine repair network.

How You Will Make a Difference
- Driving , developing and executing the industrialization of new technologies and repair qualification projects to improve product outcomes.
- Leading cross-functional coordination between engineering, sourcing, quality, and repair shops to ensure project requirements are met.
- Developing and maintaining comprehensive industrialization metrics, reporting, and pacing activities.
- Partnering with Cost-Out-Team to create robust business cases to support additional repair capabilities and secure financial validation.
- Improving turnaround times for repairs by identifying supply chain bottlenecks of Aeroderivative technology and implementing effective action plans.
- Collaborating with internal and external stakeholders to scout and partner with repair vendors.

Skills for Success
You should be a proactive problem-solver with an owner’s mindset who thrives in dynamic business environments.
- The ability to manage complex projects and deliver results across a global cross-functional network.
- The capability to analyze large datasets using digital tools to track costs and project progress.
- An understanding of the aeroderivative gas turbine repair landscape.
- An expertise in navigating internal management systems to streamline industrialization planning.
- A keen interest in driving continuous improvement and customer-centric performance.

A formal education and a Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Mathematics, Computer Science, Business, or a related field are nice to have, but we are most interested in your total experience and professional achievements within service engineering or product management functions.

Where and how you'll work
This is a permanent position based in Carrara (Avenza plant). We have a hybrid working model which gives you flexibility to work from our offices and from home.

Our Culture
Every action shapes our future. That’s why our north star is a culture of impact, where everyone is empowered to thrive and achieve.
Addressing the urgent need to build a more sustainable electric power system while improving the trajectory of climate change emissions are global priorities, and we take our responsibility seriously. That is our mission at GE Vernova: continuing to electrify to thrive and decarbonize the world. We play a significant role in leading a new era of energy.
Our technology helps generate approximately twenty-five percent of the world’s electricity today, and we are working to power the rest. If we want the future of energy to be different, then join us and be the difference. Together, we are the Energy of Change!

We're determined to be the best place to grow
We believe that strong careers are built on a variety of experiences, strong connections, and continuous development. We’re committed to providing you the tools to navigate and shape a strong career journey that aligns with a healthy work-life balance. No two careers are the same, and yours should reflect your personal and professional goals. Your people leader and trusted mentors will support you through navigating your journey.
We also prioritize fair pay, performance-based rewards, and wellbeing programs for you and your family. With opportunities to move across teams and functions, your career can keep evolving while sustainability stays at the core of everything we do.

Inclusion & Diversity
We are passionate about creating an inclusive work environment. By valuing the ideas and contributions of a diverse workforce we help inspire others to grow, succeed, and raise the bar for everyone.
As an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer, GE Vernova is committed to support disadvantaged groups whilst providing equal opportunities for both GE Vernova associates and applicants alike.
Join us at GE Vernova where results can be achieved by embracing a community of belonging.

jobs.title: Sr. Quality Operations Manager – Central Europe
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The Regional Quality Operations Manager is responsible for maintaining an effective operating rhythm for Quality & Continuous improvements across the Central Europe project portfolio.
The role drives consistency, transparency and execution discipline across project, site, supplier and portfolio quality activities. It supports that quality risks, non-conformities, cost of poor quality, audit findings, corrective actions and lessons learned are systematically identified, reviewed, escalated and closed.
Reporting directly to Region Quality & Lean Leader and working closely with Portfolio Quality Leaders, Project Quality Managers, Supplier Quality, Lean, Engineering, Sourcing, Project Management, Construction and Commissioning, the role supports the organization to move from reactive issue management toward proactive quality risk prevention.

Job Description
Key responsibilities

1. Regional quality operating system
- Develop and maintain the regional Quality operating rhythm, governance model and review structure.
- Support establishing standard quality reviews at function, portfolio and project levels.
- Support maintaining alignment between global, business, regional and project quality priorities.

2. Quality performance management
- Develop & maintain the regional quality performance dashboard and action-based reporting process.
- Consolidate and analyze COPQ, NCRs, customer complaints, audit findings, deviations, concessions and corrective-action performance.
- Support identifying trends, recurring failures and systemic risks across projects and portfolios.
- Provide fact-based insights and recommendations to regional Quality Leader.
- Ensure data quality, common KPI definitions and consistent reporting across portfolios.
- Develop meaningful leading indicators in addition to traditional lagging indicators.

3. Corrective action and problem-solving governance
- Solve problems to the root cause, think critically & support building problem-solving capabilities across region.
- Drive Lessons Learned process implementation & ensure significant lessons are read across to relevant projects, tenders (ITO), functions and portfolios.
- Support establishing a clear regional process to connect RCA, 8D, Kaizen, LL, CI and other structured problem-solving activities outcome and align with global quality team.
- Monitor root-cause quality, countermeasure effectiveness and action sustainability.
- Challenge weak problem statement & root-cause analyses and support teams to sustain corrective actions.
- Ensure that problem-solving ownership remains with the responsible business and functional teams through influencing the key stake holders.

4. Process standardization and digitalization
- Identify opportunities to simplify and standardize quality processes.
- Reduce manual reporting, duplicate reviews and non-value-adding administrative work.
- Support digital quality dashboards, workflow tools and data analytics.
- Establish standard templates, review criteria and minimum quality requirements.
- Work with global quality teams to improve common tools and systems.

5. Leadership and capability development
- Build a strong community & relationship across Project Quality Managers, Equipment Quality Managers and Site Quality teams including leadership teams.
- Support competency assessment and development planning for regional quality personnel.
- Promote proactive risk management, prevention and accountability.
- Demonstrate inclusive leadership and a strong commitment to safety, ethics and compliance.

Required qualifications
- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in engineering, quality management, operations management or a related discipline.
- Significant experience in Quality, project execution, operations or engineering within EPC, infrastructure, energy, industrial or similarly complex project environments.
- Demonstrated experience managing quality governance across multiple projects or portfolios.
- Strong understanding of NCR management, COPQ, RCA, auditing and corrective-action systems.
- Basic knowledge of ISO 9001 and quality management systems.
- Strong analytical capability and experience using operational data to drive decisions.
- Ability to influence senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams without relying solely on hierarchical authority.
- Strong communication, facilitation and organizational skills.
- Fluent English; (German or another relevant European language would be advantageous).
- Ability & willingness to travel.

Preferred qualifications
- High flexibility on taking new tasks or initiatives.
- Lean, quality auditor or recognized RCA qualification.
- Experience in high-voltage transmission, grid infrastructure, power generation or major capital projects.
- Experience with supplier quality, site quality, construction or commissioning.
- Experience managing regional or multi-country operations.
- Knowledge of project management and risk-management principles.
- Experience implementing digital quality-management or reporting systems.

Additional Information

You will be a key change agent responsible for scaling the adoption of the GE Vernova Business System across all business units. Partnering with leadership and learning teams, you will lead the development and implementation of training programs that build capability and model behaviors. Your leadership and hands-on coaching will enable teams to apply structured tools effectively to solve problems, improve processes, and drive business results.

Job Description
The Lean Leader will provide tactical and operational support within the Stafford Manufacturing facility, contributing to the development and sustainment of Lean, industrialisation, manufacturing and inventory strategies aligned with business goals.

The successful candidate will partner with site and functional leadership to drive continuous improvement and operational excellence, enabling effective supply chain and manufacturing processes, improved capacity, and reliable customer delivery.

The role will focus on areas including order entry, engineering and production scheduling, manufacturing industrialisation, production flow and cycle times, capacity improvement, visual management and daily management.

Key Responsibilities:
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives that positively impact Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost and People (SQDCP) .
- Lead and coach the implementation of site-wide Daily Management, from Level 0 through Level 3.
- Drive the application of Lean principles and methodologies, including Kaizen, structured problem solving, Moonshine projects and other continuous improvement initiatives.
- Lead cross-functional teams of hourly and salaried employees during Kaizen, Lean and Work-Out events.
- Develop and continuously improve Value Stream Maps (VSMs) to identify opportunities for process, productivity and flow improvements.
- Implement Lean Manufacturing strategies, including setup reduction, workplace organisation, standardised work, process and workflow optimisation, visual management and inventory reduction.

- Analyse operational issues and performance variances, identify root causes and implement sustainable corrective and improvement actions.
- Develop, review and maintain improvement plans, ensuring actions are followed through to measurable results.
- Work with the site Moonshine team to support production preparation and 3P activities where required.
- Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing capacity, cycle times, production flow and overall operational efficiency.
- Partner with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality and other functions to ensure Lean initiatives support wider business objectives.

- Bachelor's degree from an accredited university,preferably in Engineering, or a relevant trade qualification combined with significant hands-on manufacturing experience

- Proven experience leading Kaizen events and developing end-to-end Value Stream Maps.

- Ability to coach, mentor and influence teams to embed a Lean culture within an environment with varying levels of Lean maturity and acceptance.

jobs.title: Sourcing & Supply Chain Leader / Directeur Sourcing & Supply Chain SEMEA (H/F)
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
À propos de l’activité

PCS est un leader dans la fourniture de systèmes et de services électriques pour les applications de conversion et de stockage d’énergie, opérant dans les segments industriels et des réseaux électriques. Au sein de PCS, la région Europe du Sud–Moyen-Orient–Afrique (SEMEA) connaît une forte croissance et regroupe 1 200 collaborateurs. Elle couvre l’ensemble de la chaîne de valeur — des machines tournantes et de l’électronique de puissance aux solutions systèmes intégrées — et sert les clients tant pour les équipements neufs que pour les services. Elle constitue également un centre mondial d’expertise et d’innovation pour de multiples applications.

Job Description
*** IN ENGLISH BELOW ***

À propos du poste

En tant que Directeur Soucring & Supply Chain, rattaché(e) au Directeur Général de la région, vous intégrerez l’équipe de direction régionale en tant que responsable de la performance de la supply chain sur les quatre piliers fonctionnels : achats stratégiques pour construire des offres compétitives, achats, logistique, conformité douane et commerce international. Vous définirez la stratégie supply chain pour un environnement complexe et multi-niveaux, couvrant les équipements électriques, l’électronique de puissance, les composants de moteurs électriques et de convertisseurs, les services sur site client et autres, tout en garantissant la performance Sécurité/Qualité/Livraison/Coût (SQDC), dans cet ordre. Vous dirigerez une organisation d’environ 60 collaborateurs ainsi que des prestataires externes. Dans cet environnement en forte croissance, vous piloterez l’amélioration continue, la transformation et le développement des équipes afin de construire une organisation supply chain performante, capable de gagner auprès de nos clients et d’exécuter selon les principes SQDC.

Description du poste
MISSIONS PRINCIPALES :
Diriger et développer son équipe afin d’atteindre les objectifs suivants :

1. Sourcing stratégique
- À partir des priorités stratégiques de l’activité et de la région, définir et mettre en œuvre les priorités stratégiques de sourcing afin de soutenir les objectifs globaux de l’entreprise et de se conformer aux réglementations mondiales.

- Développer le panel fournisseurs pour les familles d’achats clés et piloter les programmes de développement fournisseurs.

- Travailler en partenariat avec l’ingénierie et la qualité pour qualifier les composants critiques, optimiser les spécifications et les nouvelles introductions en production (NPI).

- Travailler avec les usines sur les décisions make-or-buy.

- Fournir un support sourcing efficace pour développer des offres optimisées et compétitives pour nos clients, en partenariat avec les équipes commerciales ; négocier avec les fournisseurs en phase commerciale (ITO) et en phase d’exécution (OTR).

- Collaborer avec les Global Commodity Managers (GCM) pour mettre en œuvre les stratégies globales du groupe pour les commodités directes et indirectes.

- Développer les capacités de prévision à partir des données commerciales afin de fournir à l’équipe achats les données de demande nécessaires aux besoins du processus S&OP.

- Engager nos fournisseurs stratégiques via des contrats, la gestion des QBR et des événements Lean fournisseurs, dans un esprit de responsabilité partagée et de partenariat.

- Adapter l’organisation et les compétences en fonction du développement du business et des priorités.

2. Achats
- Être responsable du processus approvisionnement et garantir une exécution sans faille des contrats clients (y compris la documentation), conformément aux principes SQDC, en partenariat avec les équipes projets, services et usines.

- S’assurer du passage des commandes dans les délais, conformément aux échéances de livraison des projets.

- Garantir des programmes adéquats de relance fournisseurs et de contrôle qualité afin de sécuriser la qualité et les délais.

- Coordonner la qualification fournisseur, l’onboarding et les inspections avec la fonction Supplier Quality Management afin d’améliorer et de sécuriser notre base fournisseurs.

- Piloter la gouvernance des dépenses, le respect de la politique achats et les processus P2P soutenus par l’ERP dans toute la région.

- Mettre en place des processus S&OP pilotés par la demande afin d’améliorer la précision des prévisions et de gérer la santé des stocks sur les catégories de composants à long délai d’approvisionnement.

- Adapter l’organisation et les compétences en fonction du développement du business et des priorités.

3. Logistique et douanes
- Superviser les opérations de transport amont et de livraison aval, tant pour les projets d’équipements que pour les interventions/arrêts chez les clients.

- Gérer les partenariats avec les prestataires 3PL et les commissionnaires de transport.

- Assurer la conformité totale aux réglementations régionales et internationales en matière d’import/export, de droits de douane et de sanctions commerciales applicables ; piloter la classification des codes HS.

- Surveiller et traiter les évolutions réglementaires ayant un impact sur l’activité.

- Mettre en place un Internal Compliance Program (ICP) pour la région, en s’appuyant sur les programmes globaux.

- Adapter l’organisation et les compétences en fonction du développement du business et des besoins spécifiques des projets.

Leadership et responsabilité transverse
- Diriger, développer et inspirer une organisation supply chain performante à travers plusieurs sous-fonctions et sites.

- Être un membre clé de l’équipe de direction régionale ; contribuer au plan opérationnel annuel, à la stratégie à 3 ans et aux décisions d’allocation du capital.

- Travailler avec les équipes commerciales et sales afin d’optimiser nos solutions en termes de coûts et de délais selon les besoins clients.

- Collaborer avec les équipes Projets, Services et Opérations / Manufacturing pour assurer l’exécution SQDC.

- Piloter la digitalisation de la supply chain — optimisation ERP, portails fournisseurs, outils de prévision de la demande et visibilité logistique en temps réel.

- Présenter les KPI supply chain au Business et au Directeur Général régional (initiatives de réduction des coûts, économies, réduction du coût matière projet, COTD/SOTD, COPQ, durabilité, réduction du single/sole source, rationalisation de la base fournisseurs, contractualisation avec les fournisseurs stratégiques, DTP, respect des processus, NCR et recouvrement des réclamations).

- Développer et mettre en œuvre des plans d’action pour atteindre les objectifs KPI en utilisant la méthodologie lean/PSR.

- Développer la performance individuelle et collective de manière durable.

Profil recherché

Nous recherchons un(e) Responsable Sourcing & Supply Chain ayant une forte expérience, idéalement orienté(e) business projets, avec un parcours confirmé d’au moins 10 à 15 ans dans un poste et des responsabilités similaires.
- Diplôme universitaire ou équivalent dans un domaine lié au poste (ingénierie, économie, gestion, etc.).

- Proactif(ve) et orienté(e) processus, avec une recherche permanente d’opportunités d’amélioration via des changements de produits et/ou de fournisseurs.

- Penseur(se) stratégique capable de construire une feuille de route supply chain sur 3 ans et de résoudre simultanément une pénurie critique sur un composant à source unique.

- Présence crédible au niveau exécutif — capacité à influencer le DG, le CFO, les directeurs ingénierie, les directeurs généraux fournisseurs, et à évoluer dans un environnement matriciel.

- Décideur(se) analytique, orienté(e) données et processus, avec un biais pour la rapidité et une priorisation claire.

- Opérateur(trice) résilient(e), performant(e) dans des environnements projet, techniquement complexes.

- Capable de construire des équipes performantes et inclusives, avec un solide historique de développement et de succession.

- Expérience des systèmes ERP (SAP/Oracle) et des outils de planification supply chain.

*** ENGLISH ***

About the Business
PCS is a leading provider of electrical systems and services for power conversion and storage applications, operating across industrial and utility segments. Within PCS, the South Europe-Middle East-Africa (SEMEA) region is fast-growing P&L with 1,200 employees and spanning the full value chain — from rotating machines and power electronics to integrated system solutions — serving customers both for new equipment and services. It is also a global center of expertise and innovation for multiple applications.
About the Role
As Supply Chain Leader reporting to the region General Manager, you will join the regional senior leadership team as the accountable leader for end-to-end supply chain performance across all four functional pillars: strategic sourcing to enable competitive offering and contract execution, procurement, logistics, and customs & trade compliance. You will shape supply chain strategy for a complex, multi-tier bill of materials environment — spanning electrical equipment, power electronics, electrical motor and converter components, customer site services and others — while ensuring Safety/Quality/Delivery/Cost & Lean performance (SQDC) in that order. You will lead an organization of about 60 employees and multiple external service providers. In this fast-growing environment, you will drive continuous improvement, transformation and people development for an effective supply chain organization to win with our customers and to execute as per SQDC principles.

Main Missions:
Lead and develop his team to achieve the following:

1. Strategic Sourcing

- Adjust organization & skills in line with business development & priorities

2. Procurement

- Ensure timely placement of orders in accordance with project delivery deadlines.

- Ensure adequate expediting and quality inspection programs to secure quality & delivery

- Coordinate supplier qualification, onboarding and inspections with the Supplier Quality Management function to improve and secure our supply base.

- Drive spend governance, purchasing policy compliance, and ERP-enabled P2P processes across the region

- Implement demand-driven S&OP processes to improve forecast accuracy and manage inventory health across long lead-time component categories

- Adjust organization & skills in line with business development & priorities

3. Logistics & Customs
- Oversee inbound freight and outbound delivery operations for both equipment projects and customer site interventions/outages

- Manage 3PL and freight-forwarding partnerships

- Ensure full compliance with regional and international import/export regulations, tariffs, and trade sanctions applicable, Lead HS code classification

- Monitor and respond to regulatory changes affecting the business

- Build an Internal Compliance Program (ICP) for the region, leveraging global programs

- Adjust organization & skills in line with business development & specific project needs

Leadership & Cross-Functional Accountability

- Partner with Commercial and Sales teams to optimize our solutions for cost and lead-time based on customer requirements

- Partner with Projects, Services and Operations / Manufacturing for SQDC execution

What we are looking for:

Job Description

Job Description Summary
The US Project Procurement Leader will be responsible for building, leading, and scaling the project procurement capability supporting advanced nuclear power plant projects in the United States. This leader will oversee procurement across a broad range of project scopes, including major equipment, fabricated and machined components, engineered systems, construction-related supply and services, and other critical materials and services required for nuclear plant delivery in the U.S. market. The role requires the ability to consolidate full project procurement requirements into one cohesive approach that supports schedule performance, controls cost, mitigates risk, and delivers the best total cost for the customer.

Success in this role will require strong execution discipline, commercial acumen, supplier leadership, and the ability to operate effectively in a complex matrix organization. The ideal candidate will be equally comfortable driving day-to-day project outcomes, resolving escalations, leading cross-functional teams without direct authority, and building the procurement foundation needed to support long-term U.S. program growth.

jobs.title: Aero Alliance Lead Test Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Description Summary
The lead Test Engineer is responsible for the technical execution, data analysis, and troubleshooting of aero-derivative gas turbine testing. You will serve as the primary technical interface during the testing phase, ensuring that engines meet rigorous mechanical integrity, performance and quality standards while driving continuous improvement in test cell operations and safety.

Job Description
The Opportunity
Gas turbine performance doesn't reveal itself on a drawing — it reveals itself on a test cell. As a Test Engineer at Aero Alliance, you will be the primary technical authority during engine testing for the LM2500 and LM6000 aero-derivative gas turbine product lines. From leading test execution and analysing performance data to resolving complex mechanical anomalies and driving process improvements, your work directly determines whether an engine is cleared to operate in the field.
This is a role for an engineer who is energised by technical precision, thrives under real operational pressure, and wants their work to have a direct, measurable impact on product quality and reliability.
Key Responsibilities
- Lead test execution and analysis — execute engine testing for the LM2500 and LM6000 product lines; analyse engine performance and vibration data to verify adherence to specifications, guarantees, and mechanical integrity standards.
- Own technical troubleshooting — act as the primary technical point of contact for complex issues involving test cell systems, instrumentation, and turbine anomalies; drive root-cause analysis to resolve performance and mechanical discrepancies.
- Standardise and maintain test processes — develop and maintain test procedures covering commissioning, pre-checks, mapping, and test sequences; ensure all testing activities align with global standardisation efforts.
- Collaborate across functions — work closely with manufacturing engineering, shop operations, and G0 teams to resolve fleet-wide technical challenges and support the successful introduction of new products and processes.
- Drive operational excellence — participate in shop operational reviews; monitor and improve FPY (First-Pass Yield) and cycle time through Lean methodology and continuous improvement activity including Kaizen events.
- Communicate technical outcomes — prepare and deliver detailed technical reports for internal and external stakeholders, providing clear insights into testing outcomes and corrective actions taken.

About You
You are an experienced test engineer with a strong technical foundation in aero-derivative gas turbine systems and a track record of delivering rigorous, data-driven test programmes in complex operational environments.
Required
- Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related discipline — a formal qualification is advantageous, but we are most interested in your total experience and professional achievements.
- Proven experience in aero-derivative gas turbine testing and operations.
- Working knowledge of data acquisition systems and engine control logic.
- Ability to interpret engineering drawings and schematics accurately.
- English fluency, with the ability to communicate complex technical findings clearly to diverse audiences.
